correctness.rationale: Comparing scalar parts of the identity at (u,u) for u∈V forces the scalar part of P(u) to vanish, in every characteristic; (1,1) then forces P(1) to lie in V and gives 2L(v)=0, and (1,u) gives L²=0. Conversely these relations suffice by bilinearity on K·1⊕V. P²(1)=L(v) and P²(V)=0. Taking L=0 and v≠0 gives index two, while in characteristic two a size-two Jordan block and a preimage vector give index three; n=1 has L=0. A rank-r matrix is equivalent to a flag im L⊂ker L and an isomorphism from the quotient by the kernel onto the image, proving the Gaussian count. The centralizer has independent free block entries that clear the lower flag coordinates once an outer nonzero vector is fixed; the repeated GL_r block is required to commute with L. This gives precisely the stated orbits, including their emptiness at r=0 or n=2r, and the labelled sizes by multiplication by the matrix count. At fixed even q the exact probability is the average of q^(−r) with weights N_{n,r}. The Gaussian product has exponent 2r(n−r) up to bounded positive factors depending only on q; ranks below n/4 have exponent at most 3n²/8 while a maximal-rank term has exponent at least (n²−1)/2. The remaining terms have q^(−r)≤q^(−n/4), giving the stated uniform-in-n bound.
residual_risks: The frozen experiments cover only small prime-field cases; the reasoning above, not the experiments, checks unrestricted n and the stated fields.
